title: Quiz: The Shewhart Cycle — PDCA and PDSA

questions.text: In the PDSA cycle, an engineer runs a new algorithm on 5% of production traffic for one week and records results. This is the __ phase.
questions.explanation: Running a small-scale pilot test is the Do phase — implementing the plan on a limited scale to test the change before full deployment.

questions.text: After confirming that a new data validation script reduced errors from 2.8% to 0.4%, the team deploys it to all production pipelines and updates the documentation. This is the __ phase.
questions.explanation: Standardising a confirmed improvement (deploying to production, updating documentation) is the Act phase. If the improvement had failed, Act would mean adjusting the plan and restarting the cycle.

questions.text: The Shewhart Cycle ends once a successful improvement has been standardised in the Act phase.
questions.explanation: The cycle never truly ends — it is iterative. Each completed cycle identifies the next improvement opportunity. Continuous improvement (Kaizen) means the cycle restarts at a higher baseline.

questions.text: Which SQC tool is most directly used in the Study/Check phase of the Shewhart Cycle?
questions.explanation: Control charts are the primary tool in the Study/Check phase — they determine whether a change produced a real process improvement or just random variation.

questions.text: Deming preferred PDSA over PDCA because 'Study' emphasises understanding why results occurred, not just whether a number improved.
questions.explanation: Deming argued that 'Check' encourages a pass/fail mindset. 'Study' emphasises learning — understanding the mechanism behind the results — which enables better decisions in the Act phase.
